messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: SLO p99 latency breach detected on /v1/streaming/generate in eu-west-1 (current p99 1.9s, SLO 700ms). Auto-escalation -> paging. PagerDuty: PD-9876.

ops-bot: Symptom tags: streaming_stalls, tail_latency, kv-cache-pressure. Affected pool: kv-hot-4. Traffic spike + sustained high prefill miss rate.

tanya: ack, on it. looking at dashboards — is this coming from prefill backpressure or decode CPU spikes?

sam: I see kv cache eviction rate jumped from ~200/s to ~1.2k/s around 12:04UTC. Fragmentation metric at 72% for shard kv-hot-4. Prefill_hit_rate dropped to 18%. Decode CPU per-request jumped to 3.6 core-seconds for long sequences.

brad: confirmed streaming stalls correlate with eviction bursts. When eviction churn increases, KV prefill layer blocks and streaming flushes frames to client.

elaine: customer impact check: two paying tenants (org-alpha, org-beta) in eu-west-1 reported streaming stalls and a few reconnects. Error rate for streaming endpoints rose from 0.25% -> 2.1% in the last 15m. Notifying CSE + CS.

sre_lead: priority actions: (A) reduce prefill pressure ASAP, (B) offload some traffic to fallback pool/variant, (C) if needed, scale Dedicated capacity for kv-hot-4.

sam: quick mitigation I can apply now: flip prefill to conservative mode for eu-west-1 via console flag so prefill work is deprioritized. That should drop prefill parallelism and let decode catch up.

brad: +1. Also we should temporarily raise kv cache soft limit on kv-hot-4 so it evicts less aggressively while we stabilize. Will that require a rolling restart?

sam: soft limit change is live-update, no restart. Applying now.

[code block]
kubectl -n redwood-ops exec -it config-updater -- /app/update-config \
  --pool=kv-hot-4 \
  --set=kv.prefill.mode=conservative \
  --set=kv.cache.soft_limit_ratio=0.85
[/code block]

sam: applied both flags at 12:12UTC. Watching metrics.

ops-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE recorded: kv.prefill.mode=conservative, kv.cache.soft_limit_ratio=0.85 by sam.

sam: initial effect: prefill_parallelism down ~65%, eviction_rate down to ~420/s, fragmentation holding at ~70%. p95 improved from 420ms -> 270ms, p99 from 1.9s -> 890ms (still above SLO). Streaming stalls count cut by ~40%.

elaine: good progress. still need to bring p99 under 700ms. what's blocker? decode CPU?

sam: decode CPU for large-seq requests still high. Hypothesis: imbalance between prefill workload (prefix materialization) and decode threads — prefill is still generating KV churn due to small-key fragmentation; hot keys get evicted then re-prefilled. We need targeted eviction/compaction and to prefer decode locality.

brad: I can trigger targeted compaction on the hot shard to reduce fragmentation. It takes ~10s and is non-disruptive. Running now.

[code block]
infra-tool compaction run --shard kv-hot-4 --mode=aggressive --target-free=15%
[/code block]

brad: compaction finished at 12:21UTC. free slots up from 28% -> 46%, fragmentation down to 38%. eviction_rate dropped further to ~160/s.

ops-bot: METRIC_UPDATE: p99 now 620ms, p95 220ms, streaming_stalls trending down.

elaine: that's under the SLO for p99, but keep watching for regression. Sam, keep prefill conservative for 30m and we'll plan a follow-up patch.

sam: setting timer and will rollback if regressions occur. Also starting gradual traffic shift of non-critical customers to fallback-model-compact for eu-west-1 to reduce decode CPU.

[code block]
route-tool shift-traffic --from=kv-hot-4 --to=fallback-compact-eu --pct=25 --duration=10m
[/code block]

sam: +25% shift started. Observing decode CPU drop for kv-hot-4 by ~18%.

elaine: on-call handoff: I'm taking over active remediation for the next 2 hours. brad, sam — please keep postmortem notes in #incidents once stabilized. I'll update customers and ops pager. sre_lead, you want to hand anything else off?

sre_lead: thanks, elaine. I'll remain available for escalation. action items: 1) run full compaction playbook on remaining hot shards, 2) investigate prefill vs decode scheduling bug in scheduler v1.9.3, 3) schedule a controlled experiment to disable prefill entirely in a canary to measure impact on throughput/latency.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty PD-9876 -> status: acknowledged by on-call. Link: https://pd.example/pd/9876 (internal). Severity: Sev2.

elaine: brief customer impact note for timeline: 12:03UTC spike detected; 12:08UTC paging; 12:12UTC conservative prefill flag applied; 12:21UTC compaction completed; 12:24UTC p99 recovered under SLO. Impacted customers: org-alpha (10% of their streaming calls saw stalls), org-beta (reconnects on long streams).

tanya: adding biz-ops note: recommend proactive email to affected accounts summarizing mitigation and upcoming safeguards. Ops to confirm wording.

brad: post-incident follow-ups I'm assigning: ticket INF-3247 (compaction automation), INF-3248 (prefill scheduling fix), INF-3249 (better shard-level circuit breakers).

elaine: thanks everyone. I'll stay on for the handover to the next on-call in 2 hours, will post a final incident timeline and impact estimate. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: transitioning to monitoring state. If p99 > 700ms for 5m, auto-reopen.

sam: note for postmortem: we observed a prefill <-> decode imbalance that amplifies fragmentation and eviction churn. Short-term mitigations: conservative prefill mode, targeted compaction, temporary traffic shift. Long-term: scheduler fix + shard-level backpressure.

elaine: copying this thread into #incidents and will start the draft postmortem. Closing active pager in 30m if stable. :wave:
